column1: # Thirty-six corpus files are encryption tests, and `tpdf` tries the empty
# password and nothing else -- which is right for a tool and wrong for a
# census. Without this file those thirty-six are abstentions inside a pass
# rate: counted as failures, attributed in docs/verification.md, and measuring
# nothing about the engine. With it, thirty-four of them are measurements.
# Every password here is STATED UPSTREAM and the fourth column says where.
# Ruling 13 forbids an outside program adjudicating a document; reading a test
# script for an INPUT is not that, and a password is an input. Two rows are
# marked `derived` because no upstream file names them -- they were found by
# trying what their siblings use, and the word `derived` is there so nobody
# Format: corpus <TAB> path <TAB> password <TAB> source. The separator is a tab
# because eight of these passwords contain spaces. Fields are not trimmed. `#`
# starts a comment; blank lines are skipped. The file is UTF-8 and three
# `path` is what the report records: relative to the corpus's own files
# TWO OF THE THIRTY-SIX ARE NOT HERE, and neither is a password:
#   is absent and 7.6.3.2's default of 40 bits applies. Algorithm 5 over the
#   empty password reproduces the file's own `/U` exactly at sixteen key bytes
#   and not at five, so the file was built at 128. Following the default and
#   qpdf/issue-147.pdf is ninety-one bytes of fuzzer output from qpdf's own
#   fuzz/ corpus: no header, `/O` and `/U` both empty strings, `/Length 160`.
#   With an empty `/U` there is nothing for any password to authenticate
# AND ONE ROW NAMES A GAP RATHER THAN CLOSING IT: saslprep-r6.pdf is pdf.js's
# test that a revision 6 password is SASLprep-normalised before it is hashed
# (ISO 32000-2 7.6.4.3.3, RFC 4013). This engine does not do that, so the row
# carries the normalised form and says so. The gap is named in
# docs/features/encryption.md; what this row buys is the rest of the file
# measured, and what it must not buy is a missing feature looking present.
